title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and made quick work of their light agenda.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and opened the floor for public comment.

Lee Beckman of Milano and Grunloh Engineers in Effingham updated the council on the city’s grant applications.

Arriel Dulaney of the Flora Chamber of Commerce then asked commissioners to close South Main Street in addition to North Avenue downtown for the Fall into Flora event on November 6 and 7. The council approved the closures but delayed them until 9 a.m. so morning school traffic can clear.

Members expected to hear from Community Navigator JoAnna Spicer of the Illinois Breast and Cervical Program about the Rev Up for Pink event at Christ’s Church this Saturday. Police Chief Jeremy Ruger told the council he had already spoken with Spicer. Officers will help with traffic control if needed. Commissioners approved the request.

The council then approved the meeting agenda and the consent agenda, which included past meeting minutes and the warrant list for the last half of September.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer praised Flora’s young athletes. She noted the Wolves football team’s win over Fairfield on Friday, the Junior High Pups’ appearance in the state quarterfinals on Saturday, and the JFL seventh- and eighth-grade teams advancing to their championship game.

She also reported that the city’s downtown grant applications have cleared one hurdle and moved to the next level, though officials gave no timeline for further action.

When Spicer polled the commissioners, Phil Wiley added his congratulations to the Pups for reaching the state baseball tournament, the JFL seventh- and eighth-graders facing Johnston City on Saturday in Albion, and the football Wolves for beating Fairfield Friday night.

City Administrator and Economic Development Director Mike Stanford asked the council to approve an ordinance conveying a tract of land at 102 East Second Street to H & S Investments, LLC. The vote was unanimous. Stanford also said work on the new police station will likely go out for bids soon.

Near the end of the meeting, Public Services Superintendent Toby Rinehart presented two items. Commissioners approved an ordinance accepting a materials proposal and awarding the oiling-and-chipping project to Mt. Carmel Stabilization for $130,573. They also approved an upgrade to the lift station at Car Corral. The original budget was $35,000; the actual cost came in at $38,507. The council approved the higher amount.

title: SHOTS FIRED ARREST
full_story:
The Effingham County Sheriff’s Office responded Sunday evening to a reported shots-fired incident in rural Mason.  An investigation determined that no firearm had been discharged.

At approximately 7:08 pm, Sunday Effingham County Deputies were dispatched after a caller reported being struck in the head and shot at during an argument on 1100th Street, in rural Mason.

Officers from the Effingham Police Department, Watson Fire Protection, Rural Med EMS, Illinois State Police and Illinois Department of Natural Resources assisted ECSO Deputies.  A drone was deployed to survey the area.  During the response, five people at a nearby property were temporarily detained after officers observed activity that raised concern about a possible weapon.  They were released after officers determined they were unarmed and not involved in the reported altercation.

Deputies later located and detained two people connected to the incident without further incident.  Investigators determined that the confrontation arose from a dispute involving a side-by-side ATV on a family farm.  Based on statements and evidence gathered at the scene, two individuals got into a physical altercation, neither individual was seriously injured.

Emergency medical personnel evaluated the injured person at the scene.  The person was not transported to a hospital.

Investigators determined that the reported weapon was a pepper-ball gun and that no firearm had been fired at anyone.  The incident was determined to be mutual confrontation, and no arrests have been made at this time.

title: WAYNE COUNTY WEST NILE
full_story:
Routine mosquito testing identified the first batch of mosquitoes positive for West Nile virus in Wayne County.

The mosquitoes were collected last Tuesday and Wednesday in eastern Wayne county.  Illinois Department of Health officials say the nearest human case of West Nile virus is in neighboring Marion County.  An 86-year-old individual from Shelby County was the first West Nile virus death this year in Illinois.

West Nile virus is transmitted through the bite of a Culex mosquito that has picked up the virus from an infected bird.  Common symptoms include fever, nausea, headache and muscle aches. Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
Entry forms for the Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade on Saturday night, October 31st at 7:00 pm are now available.  There is no theme, so entrants can use their own creativity when planning the entry.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Please register at the chamber no later than Noon on Friday, October 30th.  The Chamber office is open on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 am to 5 pm.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after Noon on Friday, October 30th.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Illinois farmers completed another 10% of corn and soybean harvest in the past week, bringing harvest totals to 36% for corn and 31% for soybeans as of Oct. 4, according to USDA.

According to the USDA there were 5 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending October 4th.  The average high temperature was 64.5 degrees, 3.5 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.21 inches, 0.5 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 24% short, and 55% adequate and 10% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 12% very short, 26% short, 55% adequate and 7% surplus.

Corn mature reached 92%, compared to the 5-year average of 88%.  Corn harvested reached 36%, compared to the 5-year average of 30%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 9% poor, 30% fair, 43% good, and 15% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 87%, compared to the 5-year average of 90%.  Soybeans harvested reached 31%, compared to the 5-year average of 29%.  Soybeans condition was rated 4% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 44% good, and 14% excellent.

Winter wheat planted reached 15%, compared to the 5-year average of 16% with 2% emerged, compared to the 5-year average of 4%.

title: SURGEON LAUREN WILLIAMS, CONFERRED
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital announced that Lauren Williams, MD, FACS, General Surgeon, was recently conferred into the FACS (Fellow of the American College of Surgeons) during the American College of Surgeons Clinical Congress in Washington, D.C.

The FACS designation represents a significant professional accomplishment.  According to the American College of Surgeons, earning Fellowship involves a rigorous application process that includes verification of credentials, review of a surgeon’s case log, recommendations from colleagues, and an interview conducted by a panel of experts.  These requirements are designed to ensure that Fellows meet and uphold the College’s standards for surgical care and ethics.

The American College of Surgeons states that the FACS designation indicates that a surgeon’s education and training, professional qualifications, surgical competence, and ethical conduct meet the high standards established by the College.

“We are extremely proud of Dr. Williams and this significant professional accomplishment,” said Andy Flemer, CEO of Fairfield Memorial Hospital.  “Her dedication to her patients and commitment to providing exceptional surgical care are tremendous assets to Fairfield Memorial Hospital and the communities we serve.”

The American College of Surgeons is a scientific and educational organization of surgeons that works to improve the quality of surgical care by establishing high standards for surgical education and practice.

Dr. Williams provides general surgical services at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, where she practices alongside Thomas Vaskekas, MD, General Surgeon, and Misty Stone, APN, FNP.  Together, they provide patients throughout the region with access to surgical care close to home.

title: POSTAL DEADLINES
full_story:
The US Postal Service released its recommended mailing and shipping deadlines for customers ahead of the 2026 holiday season.

For expected delivery before December 25th within the contiguous United States, USPS recommends sending items by December 17th for USPS Ground Advantage and First-Class Mail, December 18th for Priority Mail and December 19th for Priority Mail Express, the website said.

For Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and US territories, the recommended deadline for USPS Ground Advantage is December 16th.

The recommended dates are December 17th for First-Class Mail, December 18th for Priority Mail and December 19th for Priority Mail Express.

The Postal Service recommends that customers mail and ship packages early during the holiday season to help ensure arrival by December 25th.

A complete list of recommended mailing dates for packages being sent to military and international addresses is expected to be available on the USPS holiday shipping website beginning in mid-October.

title: LAKER VISIT DAY
full_story:
Lake Land College will host Laker Visit Day on Monday.  The event is designed for prospective students to learn about programs, opportunities and resources available at Lake Land College.

During the event, attendees will have the chance to tour campus with current Lake Land students, who will share insights and provide a valuable student perspective on the College.  Attendees will also meet with faculty to ask questions, discuss career plans and learn about specific programs of interest.

Attendees will also be able to learn more about the many services and student resources available at Lake Land College, with representatives from Counseling Services, Career Services, Student Accommodations, Student Wellness, TRIO Student Support Services, Financial Aid and more available throughout the event to provide information and answer questions.

Check-in for the event will begin at 8:15 am in the Luther Student Center, with the event starting at 9 am.

Attendees are also welcome to bring their parents or guardians to the event.  A special session will be offered to provide information relevant to parents or guardians of future Lakers.

“If you’re thinking about coming to Lake Land or just trying to narrow down college options, Laker Visit Day is the perfect way to get started,” Pam Hartke, Associate Dean of Recruitment & Enrollment Management, said.  “There’s no better way to discover what college life here is like than by experiencing it yourself.”

For more information or to register, visit the Lake Land College visit page at LakeLandCollege.edu/visit.

title: TRANSIT AGENCIES FUNDING
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation and the Illinois State Board of Education announced a formal notice of funding availability for eligible agencies to establish programs that encourage and support public school students to use transit outside of the Chicago area.  A total of $35 million is available via a competitive grant process, with applications due October 15th.

The Downstate Reduced Fare Grant Program and the Downstate Cooperative Transportation Grant Program are the result of legislation passed by the General Assembly this year.

Available to transit agencies outside the territory covered by the Northern Illinois Transit Authority, the programs are designed to provide additional and affordable transportation options for students enrolled in public schools and increase access to transportation for school, extracurricular and other activities.

The Downstate Reduced Fare Grant Program is open to public transit agencies to establish, continue or expand their own free or reduced fare programs for eligible students in public elementary, middle and high schools or enrolled at career centers and public technical education centers administered by ISBE.  The program is intended to supplement existing transportation options for students by making transit more affordable, while reimbursing transit agencies for providing free or reduced fares.  A total of $20 million through IDOT will be awarded to successful applicants.  Grants will be administered in five-year cycles.

The Downstate Cooperative Transportation Grant is offered to transit agencies to establish, expand or coordinate student transportation services in partnership with public schools and regional offices of education as well as career centers and public technical education centers administered by ISBE.  Eligible activities include transportation planning, scheduling, service coordination and eligible equipment and other costs associated with providing student transportation services.  A total of $15 million is available.  Grants will be administered in five-year cycles.

Applications should be submitted online through IDOT’s transit grant management system at ildot.blackcattransit.com.  Awards will be announced in early 2027.

To explain the funding opportunity and how to apply, IDOT is hosting an informational webinar on September 22nd, at 3 pm.  Registration may be completed for the September 22nd at https://idot.click/nofo-092226.

For more information, contact IDOT’s Bureau Chief of Transit Operations David J. Schafer at [email protected]. ​
